title: Gravity-induced wavefunction collapse: testing Penrose's proposal
bottleneck: Roger Penrose proposed that superpositions of different spacetime geometries are unstable and collapse on a timescale set by their gravitational self-energy, tying the measurement problem to quantum gravity. The predicted collapse times for achievable masses are far longer than environmental decoherence times, making the effect extremely hard to isolate.
why_it_blocks: This is one of the only proposals linking the measurement problem to quantum gravity with a quantitative prediction; testing it would probe both problems at once, while failure to test it leaves the link speculative.
current_state: Related Diósi-Penrose models are constrained by underground experiments searching for anomalous X-ray emission from spontaneous collapse, progressively narrowing but not closing the viable parameter space. The Diosi-Penrose model predicts anomalous heating and X-ray emission that underground detectors constrain, steadily shrinking the viable collapse parameters.
